native_result.query: At what Socioeconomic levels is the advantage in completion rates for Black students more pronounced?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students becomes more pronounced at higher SES levels indicated by a positive interaction term SES*is_Black(coefficient:0.6271 (significant))
native_result.HypoB: When controlling for academic resources and test performance (ASVAB composite ability scores and high school class percentile rank), the advantage in college degree completion rates for Black students relative to White students is most pronounced at middle-to-high socioeconomic status (SES) levels. Specifically, Black students exhibit a statistically significant completion advantage in the medium SES stratum (OR = 2.13, p = 0.024) and high SES quartiles (OR ≈ 1.92–1.97), whereas at low SES levels no relative completion advantage is observed (OR = 0.96, p = 0.94).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Inspected data distributions and missing values in nls_ses_processed.csv across race, SES, test scores (ASVAB composite), class percentile rank, family size, and BA degree completion. 2. Stratified sample across SES quantiles (terciles, quartiles, and deciles) and calculated empirical completion rates by racial subgroup. 3. Estimated multivariate logistic regression models with SES-by-race interactions, both unadjusted and adjusted for academic ability (ASVAB composite), class standing percentile, family size, and sex. 4. Fitted stratified logistic regression models within each SES stratum to assess the adjusted odds ratios and p-values of Black student BA completion relative to White peers. 5. Synthesized statistical findings into a grounded natural-language hypothesis answering the research question.
